basis: Dallas Semiconductor went public on the NYSE in 1987 (encyclopedia.com company history). Its founding capital in 1984 came from Southwest Enterprise Associates, whose general partners are C. Vin Prothro, the company's chairman since 1984 (1995 proxy), and NEA Partners Southwest, which files from NEA's Baltimore office with Charles Newhall signing (SEA's 13G of 2000-02-14, EDGAR CIK 729085). Decisions D1 lists Southwest as an external affiliate run by its own team in Dallas (the Chemicals & Materials reading), so SEA's 1984 money is not NEA's; no NEA fund or partner appears in the company's filings before the listing, and the firm dates NEA's own entry 1990, labelled Public/PIPES. Flag: if Erik reads SEA as an NEA sleeve (the Spectra test: an NEA Partners entity at NEA's office as general partner), this row is a member from 1984, round not named. X1: a listed purchase (decisions.md); if Erik rules a PIPE a venture entry, this row enters at Growth.
